lines.text: Everybody being kind from the outside - that sentence is in every letter I've ever gotten, so let me answer the whole letter. Groups exist: the big investigator networks have kept regional contact lists since the 1980s - the abduction researchers learned early that their witnesses needed each other more than they needed researchers. You call the network, you ask for the nearest contact, and once a month there's a room where 'I lost Tuesday' isn't a confession - it's an introduction. How to tell a good room from a bad one: in a good one, nobody pushes your story further than you want to go, and nobody stops you from going further. A bad one needs you to believe exactly as much as they do. And the third door: a therapist. Not to convert you - to sleep you. A good one doesn't have to believe the lights to treat the three in the morning; they just believe the fear is real. Because it is.

You call the network, you ask for the nearest contact, and once a month there's a room where 'I lost Tuesday' isn't a confession - it's an introduction. How to tell a good room from a bad one: in a good one, nobody pushes your story further than you want to go, and nobody stops you from going further. A bad one needs you to believe exactly as much as they do. And the third door: a therapist. Not to convert you - to sleep you. A good one doesn't have to believe the lights to treat the three in the morning; they just believe the fear is real. Because it is. Leave nothing out.
